o1.biggest_strength: Targets the tier 3 RTO money and the 44% order-status chat load head-on, with a pincode-graded confirm flow and shipped/out-for-delivery templates that stop the 'where is my order' flood.
o1.biggest_mistake: Quiet hours set at 9 pm to 9 am clash with the after-hours data (31% of chats 8 pm to midnight); silence from 9 pm may annoy evening buyers, and the agent shift change is mentioned but not fully costed.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Keep the evening window warmer (auto-reply plus the 2 pm-midnight shift actually resourced), swap the placeholder exchange wording, and add a sample approved template with real variables so it is literally paste-ready.

o2.biggest_strength: The ₹30 prepaid break-even logic (only worth it above 17% RTO, so metro gets nothing) is sharp owner-grade thinking, and the scripts sound genuinely like Snitch with natural Hinglish.
o2.biggest_mistake: Aggressive tier 3 auto-cancel after 48 hours with no call risks losing real delivered sales and goodwill, and the cart-volume maths (42,000 ÷ 0.7) is shaky.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add a light call or WhatsApp fallback before cancelling tier 3 orders, show the RTO cost split by pincode group explicitly, and tighten the cart-recovery sizing numbers.

reason: Output 1 is more complete and owner-ready, with pincode-graded flows, the RTO rupees laid out by group, and a fuller scorecard, while Output 2 has the cleverer prepaid break-even and warmer voice but risks auto-cancelling good tier 3 sales.
